bib.title: Simple and Effective Multi-Paragraph Reading Comprehension
bib.venue: ACL 2018 (56th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Long Papers)

question: How can a paragraph-level QA model be adapted to document-level or multi-document input without being distracted by irrelevant paragraphs?
hypothesis: Models trained only on answer-containing paragraphs give poorly calibrated, non-comparable confidence scores across paragraphs; training on sampled non-answer paragraphs with a shared-normalization objective will fix this.
contributions: An improved pipelined method (linear TF-IDF paragraph selector, summed objective for noisy distant labels, refined BiDAF+self-attention model)
A confidence method that samples non-answer paragraphs and uses a shared-normalization objective so per-paragraph scores are comparable
State of the art on TriviaQA web and wiki by about 10 points, plus document-level SQuAD, TriviaQA unfiltered and Curated TREC results
Released code and an end-to-end demo

method.summary: A BiDAF-style paragraph reader with self-attention is trained with a summed (marginalised) start/end objective over distantly supervised answer spans. For multi-paragraph input, several paragraphs per context (including ones without answers) are sampled per batch and span scores are softmax-normalised jointly across them (shared-norm); at test time the highest pre-softmax span score over all paragraphs wins.
method.task: extractive reading comprehension / open-domain QA over documents

datasets.name: TriviaQA web
datasets.source: Joshi et al. 2017; question-document pairs from web search where document contains the answer
datasets.preprocessing: consecutive paragraphs merged up to max size 400 (600 in training and 800 at test for final model) with learned separator tokens; all spans matching the official evaluation script's exact match marked as answer spans

datasets.name: TriviaQA wiki
datasets.source: Joshi et al. 2017, Wikipedia articles only

datasets.name: SQuAD (document-level)
datasets.size: 500 random training questions hand-labelled for context dependence
datasets.preprocessing: all paragraphs of an article concatenated into one document

datasets.name: Curated TREC
datasets.split: test only, no retraining on its train questions

models.name: Clark and Gardner model (BiDAF + residual self-attention, GRUs)
models.architecture: GloVe 300d + char-CNN embeddings, shared bi-GRU, BiDAF attention, residual self-attention layer, bi-GRU start/end prediction

other.no_answer_head: two layer network with 80 dimensional hidden layer, ReLU

training.objective: summed NLL over all answer-start (and end) tokens, -log(sum_{a in A} p_a); shared-norm softmax across paragraphs of the same context (alternatives: merge, no-answer option, sigmoid)
training.epochs: 26 epochs on SQuAD in under five hours
training.seq_len: paragraph max 400 (600 for final TriviaQA training)
training.dropout: variational dropout 0.2 on input to all GRUs and attention mechanisms
training.regularisation: exponential moving average of weights, decay 0.999, used at test time; word vectors not updated
training.wall_clock: 26 epochs SQuAD in less than five hours (hardware unstated)

other.sampling: top 4 TF-IDF-ranked paragraphs (8 wiki, 16 unfiltered); 2 sampled per epoch; highest-ranked answer-containing paragraph sampled twice as often; merge and shared-norm require at least one answer paragraph and both in the same mini-batch

inference.decoding: most probable answer span of length <=8 (TriviaQA) or <=17 (SQuAD); across paragraphs choose highest un-normalised span score (start score + end score)
inference.retrieval: single doc: smallest TF-IDF cosine distance; multi-doc: linear classifier on TF-IDF score, first-in-document flag, preceding tokens, question-word count. TREC demo: up to 10 Bing web documents plus TAGME-linked Wikipedia articles, top 16 paragraphs

parameters.paragraphs_at_test: 1 to 15 for TriviaQA web/SQuAD, up to ~30 unfiltered

metrics.name: EM
metrics.definition: exact match under official evaluation script

eval.protocol: dev ablations and published test sets; no significance tests or seeds reported

limits: Authors concede SQuAD questions are not built to be answered independently of their paragraph; about 10% are paragraph-dependent and ambiguous at document level.
TREC comparison with DrQA and YodaQA is across different corpora and training data, so authors disclaim claims about individual components.
Chen et al. document set has articles edited since the questions were written, so some questions may be unanswerable.
Rankings across methods are read from line plots; no seeds, variance or significance tests are reported; learning rate and hardware are not stated.
Does not use evidence aggregation across paragraphs; authors say integrating it could improve results.
Dated: LSTM/GRU reader with GloVe, superseded by pretrained transformers; leaderboard comparison made 5/01/2018.

terms.definition: paragraphs from the same context use a shared normalization factor in the final softmax operations, forcing scores to be comparable between paragraphs
apply the model to multiple paragraphs and return the answer with the highest confidence (pre-softmax span score)
